correctness.rationale: The fully reconstructed finite proof establishes all implications: no singleton except dictators, pairwise-intersecting winning pairs reduce to stars/triangles, exact pivotal counts exclude each nonempty case under both indices, balanced complementary triples correspond exactly to 5-cycles, and orbit/stabilizer counts yield 12 and transitivity. A standalone independent exact integer enumeration checked all 2640 nondictatorial rules plus analytic dictator exclusion. No probabilistic or unbounded experimental inference is used.

originality.rationale: Relevant current literature proves existence of Icos and power-index formulas, not that all six-voter neutral monotone rules fair under either index are the same twelve transitive Icos copies. The new implication and five-cycle bijection are established by the supplied full proof. Historical all-six-family enumerations pose a named, non-negligible priority risk because not all their primary texts were accessible; no checked accessible result decisively covers the statement.
residual_risks: Meyerowitz (1995) complete six-element maximal-intersecting-family classification may imply the special regular-family uniqueness; full text inaccessible in the current review.

Unindexed equivalent work cannot be excluded; a same-author review is not independent verification.

value.rationale: The contemporary literature asks which electorate sizes support fair deterministic tie-free voting while distinguishing weak pivotal-index fairness from stronger voter symmetry. At the smallest even size admitting fairness, the result establishes a complete unexpected collapse of these notions and classifies every rule using an intrinsic five-cycle. This is a motivated structural equivalence and natural full classification, not merely a restatement of Icos existence or an arbitrary table entry.
